item.aggregated_output:
---
name: digest-doc
description: "Digest a document the business already has into a page-sourced fact-sheet. One family: article - anything written down, from a supplier agreement to a printed procedure to a web page. Use on digest this, summarize this document, or a document the owner hands you."
argument-hint: <file-path-or-url-or-pasted-text>
---

# Digest Document

> Turns a source document into a navigable descriptive fact-sheet so nobody re-reads the original except for legal review. Every fact page/section-sourced. Digest captures ALL substantive content of the document; decision-relevance ("implications") is a dedicated section at the end, NOT the keep/cut filter. Length: as long as the content requires — no size bands. Document families plug in as reference sets; the spine (classify → schema → full read → write → verify → file + index) is family-agnostic.

**Where `library/` is.** Every `library/…` path in this skill is inside the `apprentice-workspace`
plugin, not in your repository: `library/` is the folder two levels above this skill's own folder.

## Families

| Family | Status | Covers | Refs |
|--------|--------|--------|------|
| `article` | LIVE | Anything the business already has in writing, and anything you read to understand their field: reports, manuals, policies, white papers, web articles | `references/article-*.md` |
| books | OUT OF SCOPE | Long-form books — different mechanics | not this skill |

New family = one schemas ref + one importance ref + one gotchas ref + eval baseline; update `--family` values in the frontmatter hint.

## Inputs

- `<file-path-or-url-or-pasted-text>` — the source document, workspace-relative or absolute; the article family also accepts a public URL, **pasted text**, and a **batch of several articles in one message** (digest each separately, one file each). If missing, ask user.
One family ships, `article`. If a document does not fit it, STOP and report - propose what the new family would need, do not force this schema onto it.

No other arguments. The type within the family (paper / report / page) is always inferred from the title page and filename — state the inference in the report. Output path is always the source document's directory, named `{doc-date}_{doc-slug}-summary.md` (doc-date = issue/submission/document date from the title page, NOT today). Exception: URL-sourced articles have no source directory — filing home + naming per `references/article-schemas.md` § Filing home.

## Step 0 — establish WHERE you are, before anything else

```bash
git rev-parse --show-toplevel          # -> the root of the repository you work in
```

**User-level since 2026-07-27**, so this runs in every workspace and must never assume one. Whatever
this prints is the repository, and its `apprentice-workspace/` folder is the workspace the digest is
filed into. Exit 1 → **stop and report**; do not guess a root, do not fall back to cwd. Filing routes
are in `references/routing.md`; there is deliberately no destination flag (preference #17 rule 2 —
config is read from the workspace, not typed).

Do not hand-roll the check. "Walk up to a directory with `.git/`" is true in both workspaces and in
every worktree, and silently resolves the wrong root.

## Workflow

1. **Classify.** Read document page 1 (and the table of contents if present) and infer the type within the article family. A document that fits no type is a STOP, not a forced fit.
2. **Load the family spec.** Read `references/{family}-schemas.md` (section template for the type) and `references/{family}-importance-rules.md` (keep/cut/must-keep-verbatim rules). Do not digest from memory of a previous run.
3. **Read the full document** in ≤20-page chunks. No skipping: boilerplate pages get skimmed for unusual clauses (see gotchas), not skipped.
4. **Write the digest** per the type schema: YAML frontmatter (`title, solicitation/identifier, class: Immutable, sensitivity, style: descriptive, source, updated`), then schema sections. Every fact carries a `p.N` / `§N` source. Tables over prose.
5. **Verify.** Spot-check ≥5 high-stakes facts (dates, dollar figures, page limits, clause obligations, names) against the pages cited. Confirm every must-keep category (deadlines, eval factors, deliverables, IP/ownership clauses, qualifiers) appears. Fix before filing.
6. **File + index.** Resolve the output path per `references/routing.md`. **Writing the file is the default, never optional**: a digest costs a full read and often a paid fetch, so leaving it in the chat loses it. Add a row to the directory's `INDEX.md` (class Immutable, same sensitivity) in the same operation. Report: family + type used (stated vs inferred), output path, section count, verification result, any flags raised.

## Gotchas

Top four inline; full per-family list in `references/{family}-gotchas.md` — read it at step 2.

- **Dropped qualifiers flip obligations.** "Virtual unless CO approves in writing" digested as "virtual" turns a conditional into an absolute. Keep every qualifier verbatim.
- **Unusual clauses hide inside boilerplate.** A section that looks standard is where the one non-standard term hides — the clause nobody reads is exactly where an obligation gets added. Skim all boilerplate for deltas from the prior or sibling version; digest only the deltas.
- **A reply document answers "what did we commit to," not "what were we asked."** The wrong default is re-summarising the request the reply echoes back. Correct: a commitments table — promise, the requirement it answers, the page.
- **Wrong-family forcing.** A document that fits no live family — a book, a slide deck, a transcript — squeezed into the nearest schema produces a broken digest. Correct: stop, report, and propose the family rather than forcing it.

## Constants

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| Skill location | `library/skills/digest-doc/` in the `apprentice-workspace` plugin, reached through the plugin |
| Workspace probe | `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. **Local patch for the apprentice workspace:** upstream this skill probes a script that recognises exactly two GitRoll repositories by git remote and exits 1 on anything else, which halted this skill at step 0 here |
| Filing routes | `references/routing.md` — per-workspace destinations, read at runtime |
| Family refs pattern | `references/{family}-schemas.md`, `references/{family}-importance-rules.md`, `references/{family}-gotchas.md` |
| article refs | `references/article-schemas.md`, `references/article-importance-rules.md`, `references/article-gotchas.md` |
| Reference outputs (proven format) | Held in GitRoll's own workspaces and not shipped here. The schemas in `references/` are the contract; follow those |

## Output

One markdown fact-sheet next to the source document (URL-sourced articles: in the topical research directory) + one INDEX.md row. Structure per the family schemas ref. Frontmatter `style: descriptive`.

## Style

- Style directive: descriptive fact-sheet (`library/sops/working-standards.md`) — no intro, no narrative, no persuasion; facts, tables and lists; no emojis.
- Tested on: a frontier model. Smaller models drop page citations, which is the whole point of the output.
- Model floor: Sonnet 4.5 — below that, qualifier preservation and page-citation accuracy degrade (untested; floor is a judgment, re-eval on first sub-Sonnet run).

## Eval

**No baseline pair ships with this copy.** Upstream, this skill is evaluated against two worked
examples; both were built from GitRoll's own federal contract documents and internal research filings,
so neither travels. Until a replacement pair exists, judge a digest against the acceptance criteria
directly: every must-keep category present, at least five spot-checked facts matching their cited
pages, every qualifier intact, and decision-relevance confined to the implications section.

Building the first apprentice-side baseline pair — one input document, one accepted output — is a good
first contribution to this library.

## Quality Guidelines

Adhere to:
- `library/reference/agent-quality-guidelines.md` (runtime behavior)
- `library/reference/skill-architecture.md` (structural principles)

`library/` here is the plugin's library: the folder two levels above this skill's own folder.
# Project E — Practitioner Credentialing Interview

Participant: Beckham Vo · Exported: 10/21/2026, 5:51:44 PM

## Renata Kowalczyk · Medical Services Professional, Medical Staff Office

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:22 PM

Can you tell me a bit about yourself and what you do for work?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:22 PM

I am the Medical Services Professional at Larkhollow Community Hospital. I run the initial-appointment credentialing file here on my own, from the day an application arrives to the day privileges go active, and I would like that run to be something a tool does rather than something I hold in my head. The part that costs me most is the waiting. A file sits ready for the committee for weeks while a licence expires underneath it or a peer reference passes its two-year signature date, and I only notice when I happen to look. The rest is bookkeeping I am doing by hand—three requests per source, every attempt logged, a thirty-day clock on every letter I send an applicant, and a packet that has to be tied to one exact revision of one application. A good place to start is how a file actually moves from intake to active privileges. Ask me about whichever part you want to build first and I will go into the detail.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:22 PM

What type of business are you running?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:22 PM

I'm not running a commercial business; rather, I operate the Medical Staff Office at Larkhollow Community Hospital. My role is to manage the initial credentialing process for licensed practitioners, verifying their qualifications and preparing their files for review by the medical staff committees and the Governing Body.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:23 PM

What would a procedure look like? From a day-to-day basis for your work?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:23 PM

On a day-to-day basis, I start by reviewing new application revisions for completeness, ensuring all required documents and authorizations are present before sending verification requests. I also check returned verifications against the submitted information, manage the thirty-day clocks for missing items, and track the attempt log for every source. For the specific rules governing this workflow, you can refer to the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure (LARK-MSO-2026.1).

- [Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure (LARK-MSO-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:24 PM

What are the office forms and how do you complete it?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:24 PM

We use two main forms: the Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges and the Professional peer reference form. I send the application to the applicant to complete and return, and I send the reference form directly to their referees. You can review the details in the Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges — blank form and the Professional peer reference — blank request and return form.

- [Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges — blank form (LARK-APP-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)
- [Professional peer reference — blank request and return form (LARK-REF-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:25 PM

Can you tell me what the Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges form is?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:25 PM

It is the form applicants complete to provide their professional and educational history, declare their licences, list peer referees, and answer professional practice questions. It also contains the Authorization and Release. You can read the details in the Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges — blank form.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:25 PM

What is the Authorization and Release?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:25 PM

The Authorization and Release is a critical form that the applicant signs to permit us to verify their credentials. It serves as the gateway for all verification requests; until a signed release is on file, I do not send any requests at all. You can find the rules regarding this in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

- [Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure (LARK-MSO-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:26 PM

Then what is the Professional peer reference form?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:26 PM

It is a form I send directly to a nominated peer referee to evaluate the applicant's clinical competence, character, and professional judgment. The referee must confirm they meet certain eligibility conditions and return the form directly to me. You can find the specifics in the Professional peer reference — blank request and return form.

- [Professional peer reference — blank request and return form (LARK-REF-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:26 PM

Are there any registries? Form that I need to know or any.

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:26 PM

Registries regarding controlled substances and other checks are done outside this initial appointment verification procedure. My scope focuses only on licensure, experience, time gaps, professional education, board certification, and peer references.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:27 PM

What makes a person eligible for credentials?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:27 PM

For an applicant to be eligible, the file must meet our nine completeness conditions at intake, which includes a signed Authorization and Release and a specific privilege request. Without the signed release, I cannot send any verification requests. You can find all completeness conditions listed in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:27 PM

What are the three closed batches?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:27 PM

The three closed batches correspond to the export dates of March 16, 2026, April 20, 2026, and May 18, 2026. Each batch is a static snapshot of the credentialing records within its covered window, and once created, the batch is never edited or updated.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:28 PM

Are there documents or links for these batches?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:28 PM

Yes, all the case records are available in the Case records export folder.

- [Case records export folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:28 PM

Can you tell me what that folder does, the case records?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:28 PM

That folder contains sub-folders for each export batch. Within each batch folder, you'll find a README stating the export date and the window it covers, followed by thirteen comma-separated files and three document folders containing the formal records.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:29 PM

How should each source be read and which version governs?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:29 PM

Each source must be read according to the version in force on the decision date. For instance, the procedure LARK-MSO-2026.1 governs the process and applies the rulesQuoted from the manual alongside our own Larkhollow rules. You can read specific rules in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure and My export note.

- [Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure (LARK-MSO-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)
- [How this office exports its credentialing records (office note, 2026-03-16)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:29 PM

What are the required items for applicants?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:29 PM

Applicants are required to submit nine completeness conditions, including a signed application, our signed Authorization and Release, a privilege request, a current CV, and contact information for peer referees and verifications. You can find these in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:30 PM

What counts as the application being completed?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:30 PM

An application is considered complete when it meets all nine completeness conditions at intake, which includes the signed application, our signed Authorization and Release, a privilege request, a current CV, and contact info for peer referees and verifications. You can find these conditions in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

- [Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure (LARK-MSO-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:30 PM

What are the applicant deadlines and what happens when deadlines expire?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:30 PM

An applicant has thirty calendar days to respond to a written request for missing items, with the deadline day included. If the deadline passes with no reply, the application is considered incomplete and ineligible for processing. You can find these rules in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:31 PM

What about missing item notices?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:31 PM

If an applicant receives a notice for missing items, a thirty-day calendar clock begins on the date of the request. If the deadline passes without a response or a completed revision, the application is considered incomplete and ineligible for processing.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:31 PM

What are the rules for the licensure?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:31 PM

We verify all active and inactive professional medical licenses. Our bylaws require one current, active, full, and unrestricted license issued by the State of Washington. Any restrictions, such as probation or supervision, are reported as a finding to the Clinical Director. You can find more details in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

- [Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure (LARK-MSO-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:32 PM

Our office is in the State of Washington. Is there any law that differs from other states that we need to know about?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:32 PM

Yes, unlike federal facilities that might accept a license from any state, our bylaws require one current, active, full, and unrestricted license issued strictly by the State of Washington. You can review these requirements in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:32 PM

What is the six verification elements that we need to know about?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:32 PM

The six verification elements are licensure, experience, time gaps, professional education and post-graduate training, board certification, and professional peer references. You can find the details for each in the Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure.

- [Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure (LARK-MSO-2026.1)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit)

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:33 PM

What would you say is the biggest pain point in your current process?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:33 PM

The biggest pain point is the waiting. Files often sit ready for the committee for weeks, and during that time, credentials like licences can expire or peer references can pass their signature date without me noticing until I happen to look.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:34 PM

What do you mean by waiting?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:34 PM

Waiting means the time a file spends completely ready for review while awaiting presentation to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and the Governing Body. During this stage, I must continue monitoring credentials that might expire or peer references that could pass their signature date before the decisions are made.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:34 PM

So you want a better way of tracking and monitoring credentials?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:34 PM

Yes, exactly. I want to stop carrying the state of every open file in my head and ensure credentials and references don't expire or go stale while awaiting committee review.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:34 PM

What makes a response unacceptable?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:34 PM

A verification response is unacceptable if it is received directly from the applicant or if the source is not listed on the accepted-source table. These must be logged, re-requested from a valid source, and raised to me.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:34 PM

What is the follow-up responsibilities from the applicant, I guess?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:34 PM

The applicant is responsible for resolving any discrepancy list I send them, either by providing a written explanation or by amending the application. They also submit new application revisions as needed.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:35 PM

What are escalation timing? Do they have thirty days?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:35 PM

The thirty-day clock applies only to the applicant's response to missing items, not to internal escalations. Escalations to the Clinical Director occur immediately whenever there is a license restriction, a high-risk finding, or a threshold eligibility question.

**Beckham Vo** · Voice · 05:35 PM

What about the disposition when a source never responds?

**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 05:35 PM

<!-- apprentice-workspace: end -->

## Project readiness guidance

For assignments under this directory, read [PROJECT_PLAYBOOK.md](PROJECT_PLAYBOOK.md) at kickoff,
when reviewing material source changes, and before acceptance or submission. Apply it to the actual
assignment and project instructions. Preserve passed submissions and historical evidence unless

# Practitioner credentialing

Build a reusable Agent Skill that runs a medical staff office's initial-appointment credentialing file from application intake to recorded appointment and active privileges.

## Start

1. Read the [full task](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit): it owns the scope, deliverables and acceptance requirements.
2. Create your own repository from [this starter](https://github.com/GitRollTraining/practitioner-credentialing) using **Use this template → Create a new repository**, then clone your copy and work there.

## Supplied files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Starting instructions and the full-task link. |
| `snapshot.schema.json` | The required shape of the per-batch snapshot your Skill writes. Validate every snapshot against it. Your implementation language and validation library are yours. |

You create the Skill, its implementation, your own checks and every output the task requires. Nothing here implements any part of the office's work.

## Before you work

**Interview rule.** You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

- Export your interview as the original Work Sim Markdown, save one final complete file per session under `interviews/`, and commit and push it with your code. Do not rewrite the export. If the export is unavailable, contact the facilitator.
- No runtime is supplied. Choose the dependencies your Skill needs and document how to install and run it.
- Complete the program's coding-session capture setup in the course before assessed work, and confirm your session is being captured after your first meaningful commit. Ask the facilitator to repair missing capture before you continue.
- Meet the stakeholder to obtain the relevant business source links and context; the facilitator supplies the interview link with the assignment. Read those online sources through the intended access route.
# Project playbook

Reusable guidance for the learner and agents preparing future assignments. Read at kickoff, after material source changes, and before acceptance or submission. Use the [kickoff checklist](#kickoff-checklist) and [submission checklist](#submission-checklist) as short gates.

These are the learner's standing workflow preferences, adapted to each assignment. Read the actual requirements first; identify any conflict rather than silently changing a required procedure. Currency, units, clocks, authorities, stages, tools, exports and submission structure are project inputs. The Project D examples below are historical cases, not defaults for another project. This file is outside Project D's passed submission; preserve passed code, authentic sources and historical evidence unless a change is explicitly authorized.

## 1. Frame the outcome before building

Read the complete assignment, public assessment criteria, repository instructions, authorized source package, complete interview exports and delivery requirements. Inspect the current installed skill catalogue; read and apply only relevant skills, recording what was used and why.

Explain the intended user, operational outcome, scope, authority boundaries, required deliverable format and observable completion conditions. Show a small example of good output before building; label a mock or proposed layout clearly. Confirm the assignment's clock, date semantics, numeric precision, rounding, units and meaning of missing values. Separate confirmed requirements, assumptions, missing definitions and learner-owned decisions.

Maintain one compact requirement-to-evidence map in an existing project document where practical. Link material public requirements to exact sources, implementation or procedure, and observable evidence. Update gaps as work proceeds; a coverage claim is not proof.

| Requirement / exact source and revision | Implementation or procedure | Observable verification / output | State / gap owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<public requirement; locator>` | `<path or action>` | `<actual result; evidence path>` | `<demonstrated, pending or blocked; owner>` |

**Ready to build:** the outcome and output example are clear, material decisions are identified, and unsupported assumptions are separated from authorized work. Ask about a material unresolved choice; keep routine and independent work moving.

## 2. Establish sufficient business knowledge

Check whether the interview and native sources establish responsibilities, authority, deadlines, exceptions, corrections, partial responses, escalation and completion conditions. For each real gap, identify the missing fact, source/revision, affected behavior, alternative interpretations, consequence, owner and next action. Distinguish absent records, missing definitions, inaccessible sources and learner decisions.

Raise prioritized topics for clarification. Do not repeat an answered topic, prescribe an interview count, or infer a missing business rule. Follow the assignment's interview restrictions. Where interviews or judgment must be learner-led, identify gaps without composing the learner's questions, answers, reasons, approvals or conversations. Preserve authentic exports in the required location and retain their history; the assignment determines session/export rules.

**Ready for the affected branch:** its governing knowledge is supported, or the branch remains explicitly unresolved under a permitted disposition. An unsent draft is not evidence of an escalation or reply.

## 3. Demonstrate the required operational lifecycle

Choose the applicable paths from intake, review, human decisions, execution, reconciliation, corrections, cancellation, partial response, recovery and closure. Mark a path inapplicable only with a reason grounded in scope. Demonstrate required behavior through actual commands or interactions, including real stop/wait/resume boundaries when required. Reconstructing final states does not alone demonstrate those transitions.

Where staged inputs or persisted state apply, verify future-information isolation, stable identities, preserved snapshots, replay behavior and missing/corrupt-state handling.

Separate the evidence provider, reviewer, approver and next action owner. A returning reviewer need not supply the missing evidence. Bind actions and decisions to the applicable subject, revision, actor and source. Reassess affected approvals and obligations when material facts change; preserve prior decisions and execution history.

Check real dependencies through shared evidence, available resources or budget, authority and obligations. Continue independent work where its prerequisites permit it. A shared reviewer or source file alone does not establish a dependency. Resolve only the facts a partial response proves; leave the other issues open. A factual repair supplies no additional approval or execution authority.

**Demonstrated:** primary records show the required transitions and their intermediate states. A complete handoff may contain owned unresolved cases where allowed; their status must remain distinct from approved, executed, paid or closed work.

## 4. Cross-check results independently

Use actual supplied records as primary demonstrations. Label synthetic fixtures and hypothetical recovery probes supplemental, with their purpose and limits. Independently derive important expected results from authorized sources; comparing two outputs from the same implementation is insufficient by itself.

Inspect the actual final reports, files, screens and exports in their required form. Check amounts or quantities, identities, revisions, decisions, statuses, obligations, owners, missing information and next actions across outputs. Use focused regression checks after meaningful changes and an applicable end-to-end check before acceptance. Repeat broader checks when changes, failures or unresolved risk justify them.

**Verified:** each material requirement has an observed result and evidence that supports its scope. Record unrun checks and limitations explicitly. A successful command, schema check, test count or commit count does not establish requirement coverage.

## 5. Diagnose failure and prove recovery

Preserve the failing command or interaction, inputs, source revision, output and error. Establish the cause before changing behavior or rerunning blindly. Make a targeted correction and show a focused before/after result, followed by relevant regression checks. If a prior issue becomes resolved, require evidence for that specific issue and retain its history; unrelated issues remain independent.

Follow the project's documented recovery contract. Preserve damaged or sealed evidence; use a distinct linked reconstruction when required. Other projects may permit a different auditable recovery procedure. Repeated execution must not duplicate actions, obligations or results. Distinguish genuine operational failures from deliberately altered isolated test fixtures. Never manufacture a historical failure or success to improve a score or portfolio.

**Recovered:** observed evidence proves the identified failure is addressed and required history, boundaries and independent work remain correct.

## 6. Preserve source truth and human authority

Retain source precision, identities, provenance and history. Preserve unknown information explicitly and distinguish it from a known zero or a negative decision according to the domain contract. Reconcile conflicting sources through their established authority; do not silently override a written rule with an ambiguous statement.

Only authorized people or supplied scenario records establish approvals, exceptions and real-world actions such as payments. A definition, reply or balanced total is not automatically an authorization or proof of closure. Use the actual completion conditions.

Respect access and confidentiality rules for exports, publication and capture. Never expose credentials, protected interview prompts or restricted trainer answers; use authorized source material rather than hidden grading answers. Authentic required interview submissions follow the assignment's approved access rules. Keep restricted content out of shared reusable guidance.

## 7. Make learner participation meaningful

Use **framing** to explain the target, boundaries and quality standard; **cross-checking** to review actual evidence independently; and **resilience** to diagnose genuine failures and verify recovery. These are practices demonstrated through real work, not activity metrics.

At meaningful decisions, present the relevant source evidence, options, recommendation, reason and constraints. Record the learner's actual choice in the project's existing convention. Keep assumptions labeled. Before acceptance, show the real deliverable and a short review guide: what to inspect, what could be wrong and which judgment is needed. Distinguish “shown” from “inspected” and “accepted”; allow genuine feedback and never invent it.

Proceed with authorized routine implementation without repeated approval requests. Pause dependent work for a required missing decision or authority. Stop optional polishing when acceptance criteria are met.

## 8. Keep capture, readiness and submission traceable

Where capture is required, verify it early through an actual transcript and checkpoint, not configuration alone. Check relevant root and delegated-session payloads when applicable. Report unavailable content, redaction and accounting limitations accurately. Use supported recovery; never fabricate transcripts, lifecycle events or completeness flags.

Before submission, freeze the candidate and verify its exact version or full commit ID, required authentic exports, artifact/run/report paths, capture references and remote synchronization where required. Inspect the committed or exported bytes, not only the working copy. Review what publication exposes and obtain authorization when needed. Remote publication does not itself submit an assignment.

Give a concise readiness account: demonstrated requirements and evidence; unresolved cases with source/revision, missing fact, owner and next action; whether their unresolved disposition is allowed; implementation or verification gaps; and remaining learner actions. Report **implementation complete**, **published**, **submitted** and **graded** as separate facts. Claim submission, inspection or grading only from observed evidence or explicitly attributed learner confirmation.

## 9. Use resources proportionately

Choose tools and models with sufficient capability for the complexity, risk, privacy needs and budget. Explain meaningful cost, latency or reliability tradeoffs. Prefer bounded source reads, focused checks and existing conventions; use additional review or specialist tools where they resolve a material uncertainty. Avoid redundant broad scans and tests, unnecessary artifacts and repeated approval requests. Optimize for reliable outcomes and useful evidence, not token volume, session counts, commits or artificial demonstrations.

## Kickoff checklist

- [ ] Complete assignment, public criteria, instructions, authorized sources and delivery requirements read; relevant skills selected.
- [ ] Intended user, outcome, scope, authority, format and good-output example explained; clock and numeric conventions confirmed.
- [ ] Requirements separated from assumptions, missing knowledge and learner decisions; consequences and owners identified.
- [ ] Compact evidence map and applicable operational paths chosen, including necessary waiting, partial response and recovery behavior.
- [ ] Learner-led interview/decision restrictions and source/capture privacy requirements respected; required capture actually verified.
- [ ] Authorized work, material decision points and a proportionate implementation/verification approach are clear.

## Submission checklist

- [ ] Material changes verified with focused checks; applicable lifecycle and end-to-end acceptance demonstrated using primary records.
- [ ] Important results independently cross-checked; actual deliverables inspected and mutually consistent.
- [ ] Learner shown the real candidate and review guide; actual decisions/feedback distinguished from pending inspection or acceptance.
- [ ] Unresolved cases have sources, owners, next actions and a supported disposition; unfinished implementation and unrun checks are separate.
- [ ] Required original exports, provenance, confidentiality and historical preservation checked against this assignment's rules.
- [ ] Exact candidate/version, required paths, genuine capture and remote synchronization verified; readiness and remaining learner actions stated. Publication, submission and grading statuses are explicit.

## Project D case notes — do not generalize these rules

**Learner-confirmed outcome, recorded 2026-10-18:** first assessment 79.1/100, 68/86 checkpoints; second assessment **96.5/100, 83/86**, rounded to **97** on Passport. Individual checkpoint wording remains private. These scores do not identify which change earned which points or reveal the three remaining checkpoints. No passing score is guaranteed by this playbook.

|---|---|
| Four arrival batches required separate stopping, waiting and continuation; four reconstructed snapshots alone were insufficient operational evidence | Demonstrate the actual lifecycle and boundaries required by the next assignment |
| Project D used its fixed 2026-11-15 Europe/Amsterdam case clock, integer EUR cents, per-line decimal half-up rounding, null unknown amounts and explicit known zero | Derive numeric, date and missing-value semantics from each project's sources |
| The directory/policy defined Project D's actors, review routes and financial authority; its interview/export and submission formats were assignment-specific | Identify the next project's authorities and deliverables afresh |
| A supplemental late-transfer refund/resolution probe proved the specific issue could clear; actual C18 still lacked that recovery evidence and stayed held | Keep hypothetical recovery separate from actual case evidence; resolve only the issue proved |
| C09's employee supplied revised trip evidence while its returning reviewer retained review authority | Route repairs by responsibility rather than copying the returning reviewer as owner |
| Damaged-state recovery required a distinct linked run preserving the original | Use the governing recovery contract and retain auditable history |
| Actual C20's refund resolved overpayment in batch 3; the separate Finance requirement remained open until batch 4 | Demonstrate partial resolution and remaining conditions in intermediate states |
| The learner's authentic follow-up classified entertainment as personal under written policy; C117 became EUR40 and still awaited its claim approvals | Obtain missing business knowledge and distinguish a supported definition from a claim decision |

description: "Digest a document the business already has into a page-sourced fact-sheet. One family: article - anything written down, from a supplier agreement to a printed procedure to a web page. Use on digest this, summarize this document, or a document the owner hands you."

# Digest Document

> Turns a source document into a navigable descriptive fact-sheet so nobody re-reads the original except for legal review. Every fact page/section-sourced. Digest captures ALL substantive content of the document; decision-relevance ("implications") is a dedicated section at the end, NOT the keep/cut filter. Length: as long as the content requires — no size bands. Document families plug in as reference sets; the spine (classify → schema → full read → write → verify → file + index) is family-agnostic.

**Where `library/` is.** Every `library/…` path in this skill is inside the `apprentice-workspace`
plugin, not in your repository: `library/` is the folder two levels above this skill's own folder.

## Families

| Family | Status | Covers | Refs |
|--------|--------|--------|------|
| `article` | LIVE | Anything the business already has in writing, and anything you read to understand their field: reports, manuals, policies, white papers, web articles | `references/article-*.md` |
| books | OUT OF SCOPE | Long-form books — different mechanics | not this skill |

New family = one schemas ref + one importance ref + one gotchas ref + eval baseline; update `--family` values in the frontmatter hint.

## Inputs

- `<file-path-or-url-or-pasted-text>` — the source document, workspace-relative or absolute; the article family also accepts a public URL, **pasted text**, and a **batch of several articles in one message** (digest each separately, one file each). If missing, ask user.
One family ships, `article`. If a document does not fit it, STOP and report - propose what the new family would need, do not force this schema onto it.

No other arguments. The type within the family (paper / report / page) is always inferred from the title page and filename — state the inference in the report. Output path is always the source document's directory, named `{doc-date}_{doc-slug}-summary.md` (doc-date = issue/submission/document date from the title page, NOT today). Exception: URL-sourced articles have no source directory — filing home + naming per `references/article-schemas.md` § Filing home.

## Step 0 — establish WHERE you are, before anything else

```bash
git rev-parse --show-toplevel          # -> the root of the repository you work in
```

**User-level since 2026-07-27**, so this runs in every workspace and must never assume one. Whatever
this prints is the repository, and its `apprentice-workspace/` folder is the workspace the digest is
filed into. Exit 1 → **stop and report**; do not guess a root, do not fall back to cwd. Filing routes
are in `references/routing.md`; there is deliberately no destination flag (preference #17 rule 2 —
config is read from the workspace, not typed).

Do not hand-roll the check. "Walk up to a directory with `.git/`" is true in both workspaces and in
every worktree, and silently resolves the wrong root.

## Workflow

1. **Classify.** Read document page 1 (and the table of contents if present) and infer the type within the article family. A document that fits no type is a STOP, not a forced fit.
2. **Load the family spec.** Read `references/{family}-schemas.md` (section template for the type) and `references/{family}-importance-rules.md` (keep/cut/must-keep-verbatim rules). Do not digest from memory of a previous run.
3. **Read the full document** in ≤20-page chunks. No skipping: boilerplate pages get skimmed for unusual clauses (see gotchas), not skipped.
4. **Write the digest** per the type schema: YAML frontmatter (`title, solicitation/identifier, class: Immutable, sensitivity, style: descriptive, source, updated`), then schema sections. Every fact carries a `p.N` / `§N` source. Tables over prose.
5. **Verify.** Spot-check ≥5 high-stakes facts (dates, dollar figures, page limits, clause obligations, names) against the pages cited. Confirm every must-keep category (deadlines, eval factors, deliverables, IP/ownership clauses, qualifiers) appears. Fix before filing.
6. **File + index.** Resolve the output path per `references/routing.md`. **Writing the file is the default, never optional**: a digest costs a full read and often a paid fetch, so leaving it in the chat loses it. Add a row to the directory's `INDEX.md` (class Immutable, same sensitivity) in the same operation. Report: family + type used (stated vs inferred), output path, section count, verification result, any flags raised.

## Gotchas

Top four inline; full per-family list in `references/{family}-gotchas.md` — read it at step 2.

- **Dropped qualifiers flip obligations.** "Virtual unless CO approves in writing" digested as "virtual" turns a conditional into an absolute. Keep every qualifier verbatim.
- **Unusual clauses hide inside boilerplate.** A section that looks standard is where the one non-standard term hides — the clause nobody reads is exactly where an obligation gets added. Skim all boilerplate for deltas from the prior or sibling version; digest only the deltas.
- **A reply document answers "what did we commit to," not "what were we asked."** The wrong default is re-summarising the request the reply echoes back. Correct: a commitments table — promise, the requirement it answers, the page.
- **Wrong-family forcing.** A document that fits no live family — a book, a slide deck, a transcript — squeezed into the nearest schema produces a broken digest. Correct: stop, report, and propose the family rather than forcing it.

## Constants

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| Skill location | `library/skills/digest-doc/` in the `apprentice-workspace` plugin, reached through the plugin |
| Workspace probe | `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. **Local patch for the apprentice workspace:** upstream this skill probes a script that recognises exactly two GitRoll repositories by git remote and exits 1 on anything else, which halted this skill at step 0 here |
| Filing routes | `references/routing.md` — per-workspace destinations, read at runtime |
| Family refs pattern | `references/{family}-schemas.md`, `references/{family}-importance-rules.md`, `references/{family}-gotchas.md` |
| article refs | `references/article-schemas.md`, `references/article-importance-rules.md`, `references/article-gotchas.md` |
| Reference outputs (proven format) | Held in GitRoll's own workspaces and not shipped here. The schemas in `references/` are the contract; follow those |

## Output

One markdown fact-sheet next to the source document (URL-sourced articles: in the topical research directory) + one INDEX.md row. Structure per the family schemas ref. Frontmatter `style: descriptive`.

## Style

- Style directive: descriptive fact-sheet (`library/sops/working-standards.md`) — no intro, no narrative, no persuasion; facts, tables and lists; no emojis.
- Tested on: a frontier model. Smaller models drop page citations, which is the whole point of the output.
- Model floor: Sonnet 4.5 — below that, qualifier preservation and page-citation accuracy degrade (untested; floor is a judgment, re-eval on first sub-Sonnet run).

## Eval

**No baseline pair ships with this copy.** Upstream, this skill is evaluated against two worked
examples; both were built from GitRoll's own federal contract documents and internal research filings,
so neither travels. Until a replacement pair exists, judge a digest against the acceptance criteria
directly: every must-keep category present, at least five spot-checked facts matching their cited
pages, every qualifier intact, and decision-relevance confined to the implications section.

Building the first apprentice-side baseline pair — one input document, one accepted output — is a good
first contribution to this library.

## Quality Guidelines

Adhere to:
- `library/reference/agent-quality-guidelines.md` (runtime behavior)
- `library/reference/skill-architecture.md` (structural principles)
