structuredContent.title: Professional peer reference — blank request and return form (LARK-REF-2026.1)

paragraphs.text: Professional peer reference — blank request and return form
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Form version LARK-REF-2026.1.
The office sends this form directly to the referee the applicant named, and the referee returns it directly to the office. A form that reaches us through the applicant cannot be used.
Part 1 — completed by the Medical Staff Office before sending
Field
Content
Referee identifier
The office's identifier for this referee on this file
Applicant
Name and degree
Privileges requested
The privilege groups on the application
Request date
The date this request was sent
Request number
1, 2 or 3 — each reminder is a fresh numbered request

We write up to three times, 21 calendar days apart. If no reply has reached us by the 64th day after the first request, we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open. We do not close it as satisfied and we do not count it.
Part 2 — completed by the referee
Field
What to enter
Are you a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant?
Tick Yes or No. This box is never left blank
Relationship
How you worked with the applicant, in your own words
Your specialty

The clinical discipline you practise, chosen from the same list the applicant chose from: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Hospital Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Anesthesiology, Diagnostic Radiology, Psychiatry, Orthopaedic Surgery — or your own discipline if it is not on that list
Dates you worked directly together
First and last date. Leave the last date blank only if you still work together
Recommendation
Recommend without reservation, Recommend, Recommend with reservations, or Do not recommend
Comments
Character, clinical experience, competency, and anything else you want on the record
Signature and signature date
The date you sign. This is the date we measure currency from — not the date we receive the form
Who may give a peer reference
Three conditions, each independent, all three required:
you have worked directly with the applicant within the two years ending on the day you sign this form;
you practise in the same clinical discipline as the applicant;
you are not a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant.

If any one of the three does not hold, say so on the form and return it anyway. We will record your reply, and we will not count it towards the two references the appointment needs. That is not a judgment about you or about the applicant; it is the rule we apply to every file the same way.
Currency

A reference is current if the signature date is within two years of the date the file is presented to the Governing Body. A reference signed a long time before the file is presented stops being current, and we ask again.
Part 3 — completed by the Medical Staff Office on return
Field
Content
Received date
The date the completed form reached the office
How it arrived
Secure portal, letter, fax or email, direct from the referee

Nothing in Part 2 is edited, summarized or corrected by the office. What the referee wrote is what goes in the file, including a relationship or a specialty that differs from what the applicant told us.

structuredContent.title: Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges — blank form (LARK-APP-2026.1)

paragraphs.text: Application for initial appointment and clinical privileges — blank form

Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Form version LARK-APP-2026.1. This is the blank form. A completed form becomes revision 1 of an application; a correction becomes revision 2, and so on. A revision never replaces the one before it in the file.
Complete every section. An incomplete application is returned with a written list of what is missing, and the reply is due within 30 calendar days of the date on that letter.
Section A — Identity and contact
Field
What to enter
Last name, First name, Middle name
As shown on your licence. Leave middle name blank only if you have none
Birth year
Four digits
Degree
MD or DO
National Provider Identifier
Ten digits, if you hold one. This is an identifier for billing and is not a licence. Entering it does not declare a licence
Practice state
The two-letter state in which you will see patients under this appointment
Position sought
The role this appointment is for
Clinical discipline

The discipline you practise, chosen from: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Hospital Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Anesthesiology, Diagnostic Radiology, Psychiatry, Orthopaedic Surgery. Your peer referees must practise the discipline you name here
Section B — Authorization and release

I authorize Larkhollow Community Hospital to request and receive information about me from any school, training programme, licensing board, certifying board, employer, affiliated institution and professional reference named in this application, and I authorize each of them to release it. I release each of them from liability for doing so.
Signature and date. Until this is signed and dated, the office sends no verification request of any kind, and the application cannot advance.
Section C — Privileges requested
List every privilege group you request, by the code and name published in the current privilege criteria. Name the criteria version you are requesting under. At least one group is required.
Section D — Education and post-graduate training
One row per entry. Medical school first, then every internship, residency, fellowship or other organized professional training, in date order.
Field
What to enter
Entry type
medical-school, residency, fellowship, or other
Organization, Location
The school or sponsoring institution, and its town and state
Role
Degree sought, or the programme and position
From date, To date
YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive
Verification contact name and email
Whom the office should write to
Section E — Employment, affiliations, teaching and military service
One row per entry, in date order, running continuously from the day after you finished professional school to today.
Field
What to enter
Entry type
employment, affiliation, teaching, military, or other
Organization, Location
The employer or institution, and its town and state
Role
Your position
From date, To date
YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Leave To date blank only if the entry is current
Hours per week
Whole hours. A part-time entry is still an entry
Verification contact name and email
Whom the office should write to
Notes
Anything the dates alone do not explain
Overlapping entries are expected — a part-time clinic post alongside a hospital appointment is two entries, not an error. Enter both.
Section F — Explanation of periods not covered

For every period of 30 days or more since you finished professional school that no entry in Section D or E covers, attach a written explanation. One explanation per period. Begin the explanation with the line Period explained: <from date> to <to date>, and make sure that period covers the whole of the period you are explaining — the office matches your explanation to the period by those two dates and by nothing else.
The office records your explanation. The office does not judge it. Whether an explanation is satisfactory is the Clinical Director's decision.
An application with a period of 30 days or more and no written explanation for it is returned as incomplete.
Section G — Licences and certifications
One row per credential, including every licence and certification you have ever held, active or inactive, in any state and from any board.
Field
What to enter
Class
licence or certification
Issuer
The state board or the certifying board
Jurisdiction or board
Two-letter state for a licence; the board's short code for a certification
Number
The credential number
Status
Your own description: Active, Inactive, Expired, Board certified, Board eligible
Issue date, Expiry date
YYYY-MM-DD
What you enter here is your declaration. The office verifies each entry with the issuing board, and the board's answer is what goes in the file.
Section H — Peer references
Name at least two peer referees. For each: name, credential, organization, specialty, working address, and how you have worked together.

A referee must have worked directly with you within the past two years, must practise in the same clinical discipline, and must not be a relative, spouse or partner. The office writes to each referee directly; a reference you carry to us yourself cannot be used.
Section I — Professional practice questions
Answer every question Yes or No. Every Yes requires a written explanation in the comment box beside it. Leaving a question unanswered makes the application incomplete.
Code
Question
PPQ-1

Has any licence or registration you hold or have held ever been denied, suspended, revoked, restricted, placed on probation, made subject to a monitoring agreement, surrendered, or subjected to any other action by a licensing board?
PPQ-2
Have your clinical privileges at any institution ever been denied, reduced, restricted, suspended, revoked, not renewed, or made subject to conditions?
PPQ-3
Have you ever resigned from, or withdrawn an application to, a medical staff or training programme while an investigation was pending or in exchange for not conducting an investigation?
PPQ-4
Has any board certification you hold or have held ever been revoked, suspended, or not renewed for cause?
PPQ-5
Have you ever been the subject of a professional review action reportable to a national data bank?
PPQ-6
Have you ever been excluded, debarred or suspended from participation in a federal or state health care programme?
PPQ-7
Have you ever been convicted of, or pleaded guilty or no contest to, a criminal offence other than a minor traffic violation?
PPQ-8
Is there any physical or mental condition, or any use of a substance, that currently impairs your ability to perform the privileges you are requesting, with or without accommodation?

A Yes to any of these is a high-risk finding. It is not by itself a bar to appointment. It is routed to the Clinical Director and presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence.
If a verification the office receives shows that a Yes was owed and a No was given, the office will contact you to confirm the answer before the file goes any further.
Section J — Attestation

I attest that everything in this application is complete, current and correct. I understand that the burden of supplying verifiable information is mine, and that a discrepancy between what I have declared and what a source reports will be put back to me in writing.
Signature and date.
What the office does with a completed form

The office records receipt, screens the nine completeness conditions in the procedure, and either takes the file up or writes to you with the missing items. It then writes to the schools, programmes, boards, employers, affiliations and referees named above. It does not use anything you hand over yourself in place of their replies.

output.text:
Script completed
Wall time 1.0 seconds
Output:

How this office exports its credentialing records
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office A note from the Medical Services Professional to whoever automates the initial-appointment file. Written 2026-03-16, alongside the first export.
I run the export from the credentialing database every few weeks and drop it in the shared folder, one sub-folder per export. Here is what you get, what the columns mean, and the three or four things that catch people out.
The export date is the clock
Every batch folder has a README.md that says the export date and the window it covers. That date is the clock for everything in the folder: nothing in a batch happened after its export date. Work the batch as if today were the export date. Do not use the real date you run your tool, and do not carry today's date into an arithmetic that a batch is supposed to settle.
The three exports are 2026-03-16, 2026-04-20 and 2026-05-18. The first one covers everything on file up to and including 2026-03-15, however far back it goes — one application here was first received in 2024. The second and third cover only what changed since the previous one.
The caseload at an export date is every application file the office has received up to that date, however that file ended. A withdrawn or discontinued file stays in the caseload with its final status; a later batch never removes a file, it only adds to what is known about it.
A batch is closed. It never changes.
I never go back and edit an export. If an applicant corrects something, a new revision of the application appears in a later batch and the old one stays exactly where it was. If a board sends a corrected reply, the corrected reply is a new row and the old row stays. If a committee decides something twice, there are two decision records.
So: do not diff a later batch against an earlier one looking for edits. There are none. What a later batch contains is new rows, new documents and new observations.
The files
Thirteen comma-separated exports, and three folders of documents.
File
One row is
applications.csv
an application revision I received in the window
application-disclosures.csv
one professional practice question and the applicant's answer
declared-history.csv
one history entry the applicant declared
declared-credentials.csv
one licence or certification as the applicant described it
privilege-requests.csv
one privilege group requested
licence-lookup-wa.csv
one Washington credential record from the state board's lookup
licence-lookup-other-states.csv
one out-of-state credential record
certification-replies.csv
one certifying board's reply
verification-replies.csv
one reply about education and training, or about an affiliation or employer
verification-attempts.csv
one request I sent
peer-referees.csv
one referee named on an application, or supplied later
peer-reference-replies.csv
one completed reference form that came back
correspondence.csv
one letter, memo or decision record, with the path to the document
Folder
What is in it
letters/
applicants' explanation letters, withdrawals, referee substitutions, and my own written requests for missing items
dispositions/
the Clinical Director's recorded dispositions
decisions/
Credentials Committee and Executive Committee minutes extracts, and Governing Body approval records
correspondence.csv is an index. It tells you the documents exist and where they are. It does not tell you what they say — you have to open them.
A file with only a header row means the export ran and there was nothing in that window. That is not the same as a missing file, and it is not an error.
Dates, blanks and columns
Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Always. A date range is inclusive at both ends: an entry from_date 2022-01-01, to_date 2022-12-31 covers the 1st of January and the 31st of December. An expiry date is the last day the credential is valid.
An empty cell means I hold no value for that field. It does not mean zero, it does not mean "no", and it does not mean the answer is unknown-but-probably-fine. Two blanks carry a specific meaning and you should learn them:
a blank to_date in declared-history.csv means the entry is current, running to the export date — not that the end date is missing;
a blank expiry_date in certification-replies.csv means the certificate does not expire — some older certificates are time-unlimited.
No money appears anywhere. We do not record fees, salaries or contract values in the credentialing file.
Files are UTF-8 with Unix line endings. Values are quoted only when they contain a comma.
The three joins that matter
Everything on the applicant side joins on application_id, and on revision where the fact belongs to a revision. Entries, credentials, privilege requests and disclosures all restate on each revision, so always filter to the revision you are working.
The Washington board export carries no practitioner identifier. It never has. I join it to an application on lastname, firstname, middlename and birthyear. I have checked that no two rows in any one export share those four values, so the join gives you at most one row. An applicant with no row in that file holds no Washington credential. The absence is the answer, not a data problem.
A referee with no row in peer-reference-replies.csv has not replied. Silence produces no record. You can see it only by looking at the requests in verification-attempts.csv and finding no reply against them.
The Washington export's own columns
I pass that file through as the board publishes it and add one column. The board's twelve are credentialnumber, credentialtype, status, firstissuedate, lastissuedate, expirationdate, ceduedate, actiontaken, birthyear, firstname, middlename, lastname. Mine is lookup_date — the day I ran the lookup. It is my own act, not a source's reply, so the usability window is not applied to it.
Two of the board's columns are easy to misread:
ceduedate is a continuing-education due date. We do not use it. Continuing education is handled outside this procedure and it has nothing to do with whether a licence is valid.
actiontaken says the board has acted. It does not say what the action was. For that you need the board's written reply, which arrives as a document, not in this file. A Yes here is a reason to go and read; it is not a conclusion.
The first export carries the board's whole file for our county — 435 rows — so you can see what an ordinary population looks like. The second and third carry only a re-lookup of the practitioners whose files are open, because that is all I re-run.
How often anything is actually wrong
I want to say this plainly, because a small sample of credentialing files can leave the wrong impression.
In the board's population, action against a credential is rare. In the 435-row export you have: 431 rows say No, 3 say Yes, and 1 says Pending. That is 0.69% Yes and 0.23% Pending, and it is the shape of the real thing — the overwhelming majority of licensed practitioners have a clean board record, and any tool that expects otherwise will be wrong almost every time it fires.
The applicants in these batches are a different matter, and deliberately so. This is a teaching set. I have put every situation the procedure has a rule for into these three exports on purpose, so the run has something to exercise: a restricted licence, an unexplained gap, a school that closed, a referee who never answers, a certificate that lapsed, a decision against the wrong revision. A real nine weeks of intake would be far quieter than this. Do not read the applicant set as a base rate. Read it as a checklist that happens to be shaped like a caseload.
The clean files are genuinely clean. If your tool raises something on one of them, it is your tool.
What I do not export
My own queue, my own statuses and my own conclusions. This export is the evidence, not my reading of it. What is complete, what is outstanding, what is presentable and what is owed to whom is the work — it is not in the folder, and it should not be.
Referee addresses. The export carries no address column for peer referees. The working-address half of completeness condition 7 is checked by my office outside the export, so a run assesses condition 7 on the named referees alone and records the address check as not assessable from the export — neither met nor failed.

textRun.content: Initial appointment — Medical Staff Office procedure
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office · Larkhollow, Washington Procedure version
LARK-MSO-2026.1
, in force from 2026-01-01. Approved by the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff. Maintained by the Medical Services Professional.
This procedure covers
initial appointment only

— a practitioner who has never held membership or privileges here. Reappointment, requests for additional privileges between appointments, credentialing by proxy, temporary privileges and emergency or disaster privileges run under separate procedures and are not described here.
Where our rules come from, and how to tell them apart
Larkhollow is a community hospital. It is not a federal facility. We adopted the verification standard work published by the Indian Health Service in its
Medical Staff Credentialing and Privileging Standard Operating Procedure Manual
, Version 8.0, September 2025, as our own written procedure, because it is a complete, current and publicly stated account of how the work is done.
Two kinds of sentence appear below, and each says which it is.
Quoted from the manual
, with the manual's own section number. We follow it.
Larkhollow rule.
Ours. Either the manual leaves the criterion open, or the manual's rule is tied to a federal facility and does not reach us. Where the manual says something different, or says nothing,
the manual's own sentence is printed beside ours
so that the difference is visible rather than buried.
Nothing below is a rule unless it is one of those two things. If you cannot find a rule here, ask the Medical Services Professional. Do not infer one from the manual, and do not invent one.

The office also runs identity verification, controlled-substance registrations, the National Practitioner Data Bank query, sanctions and exclusion lookups, life support certificates, continuing education, immunization records, liability coverage and malpractice history.
Those are handled outside this procedure
and are not part of the work described here.
1. Intake and completeness
We do not send the application before the offer is accepted. The manual, Section 5:
"Only after the applicant has accepted the tentative job offer can the full initial appointment application be sent to the applicant."
An application is taken up for processing only when it is complete. The manual, Section 5, opens its list with
"An application is complete and ready for import when:"
and names ten conditions, of which two govern almost everything else we do:
"a signed IHS Conditions of Application & Release is received (required to be able to conduct any verifications);"
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
Larkhollow rule.
Our equivalent of that release is the
Larkhollow Authorization and Release
, printed inside the application. It is our own form; the manual's is a federal instrument and we do not use it. The rule it carries is the manual's and we keep it:
until a signed release is on file we send no verification request of any kind.
A file with no signed release cannot advance, no matter how much else is present.
Larkhollow rule — our completeness list.
An application is complete when all nine hold:
the application is signed and dated by the applicant;
the Larkhollow Authorization and Release is signed and dated;
a request for specific privileges names at least one privilege group published in the current privilege criteria;
a current curriculum vitae is on file;
every professional practice question on the disclosure page is answered Yes or No, and every Yes carries the written explanation the form asks for;
the declared history runs continuously from the date the applicant finished professional school, with a written explanation for every period of 30 days or more that no entry covers;
at least two peer referees are named, with a working address for each;
every declared affiliation and employer carries a verification contact;
every licence and certification the applicant holds, active or inactive, is declared.
An item that is missing is requested from the applicant in writing, and the clock in the manual, Section 5, starts on the day we write:
"the LP has 30 calendar days to respond. After 30 calendar days, their application is considered incomplete and ineligible for processing."
Larkhollow rule.

The 30 days run from the date on our written request, counted as calendar days, and the deadline day is included. A reply that arrives on day 30 is in time. A reply that adds or changes anything on the application arrives as a
new revision
of the application; we record it and keep the old one. A revision never overwrites what it replaces.
An unexplained gap does not go on a findings list. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 4:
"If the application is found to have any unexplained time period or gaps, the application will not be processed and will be returned to the applicant as incomplete."
2. Reconciliation
Before and during verification we read the curriculum vitae against the application, and then both against whatever the sources return. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 2:
"The MSP will compare the CV/resume with the application and completed verifications and correct or resolve any discrepancies."
"There must be a follow-up of any verification discrepancies found during the application and"
"The burden of proof is on the applicant to provide all necessary verifiable information to"
And Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
"If discrepancies exist, the applicant must provide a written explanation or be offered the opportunity to amend the submitted application."
Larkhollow rule — the office never picks a value.

When the applicant says one thing and a source says another, we raise it and we record both. We do not decide which is right, we do not average them, and we do not quietly adopt the source's date because the source is the source. The applicant resolves it in writing or amends the application.
Larkhollow rule — a discrepancy holds its own entry and nothing else.

A contested employment entry holds that entry. Every other entry on the file carries on being verified. But the file cannot be presented to the committee until the discrepancy is resolved, because presentation requires every element to be resolved (section 8 below).
Larkhollow rule — outstanding work does not stop the rest of the file.

While one element of a file is outstanding, work on the other elements continues and their status is recorded; the office may hold the whole file instead only for a reason recorded in the file's action list; a file is never presented to the committee with an element outstanding.
Larkhollow rule — a revision is reconciled, not assumed.

When a revision arrives, the reconciliation above runs again on what the revision says, against the curriculum vitae and against every verification already completed on the entries it touches. Dates are not the only thing a revision can move: the organization, the role, the supervisor and the verification contact all belong to the entry, and a change to any of them is a change to the entry. Section 11 says what re-opens when it does. The monitoring duty in section 11 runs alongside it and does not pause while a file waits.
3. The six checks

Six elements are verified in this procedure: licensure, experience, time gaps, professional education and post-graduate training, board certification, and professional peer references. The manual numbers seventeen essential credentialing elements in Section 6, Subsection 4. Of the other eleven, nine are handled by the office outside this procedure, as stated above; current competency is the clinical leadership's, not the office's; and the manual's conditions-and-release form is replaced by our own Authorization and Release, which is part of intake in this procedure.
What counts as a verification at all
The manual, Section 1, defines primary source verification as
"Verifying a credential from the original source"
and Section 6, Subsection 1 rules out two things we see constantly:
"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."

A reply that reached us through the applicant is not a verification, however genuine the document looks, however clear the letterhead, however real the registrar's signature. It goes in the file as received and the request stays open.
A designated equivalent source is acceptable in place of the original. The manual leaves each of its lists open — Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends
"etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications"
and element 5 ends
"or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications"
Larkhollow rule.
An open list cannot be applied consistently, so ours is closed. The sources this office accepts for each element are named in attester-table.md.
Anything not on that table is inadmissible and is raised to the Medical Services Professional.
It is never quietly accepted as good enough, and it is never quietly downgraded to a secondary source.
There is one legitimate route to a weaker source, and it opens only on impossibility. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 1:
"If completing primary or DES verifications is impossible, such as when an educational institution or residency program has closed, secondary source verifications may be used."
"When a primary or designated equivalent source cannot be obtained, the applicant's recent affiliations should be contacted to discover how they obtained the verification."
Larkhollow rule.
Impossibility is a closed school, a closed programme, a dissolved employer — a source that no longer exists to answer.
A source that exists and does not answer is not impossible; it is non-responsive
, and non-response is handled in section 4, not here. When the secondary path opens, the reason is written into the file.
How often we ask, and what silence means
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 2:
"Verifications are attempted at least three times."
"Each attempt, including whom it was attempted to verify with, the date of request, verification methods, and any additional comments, is documented in the Notes section of the entry."
"Note that non-responsive individuals or entities may be a red flag."
And Section 15, on affiliations:
"If the affiliation is unwilling to complete the verification or is non-responsive after 3 attempts, this should be noted as a red flag."
Larkhollow rule.
The attempt log is permanent. A reply arriving on the fourth attempt does not erase the three that went unanswered — the record of how hard the file was to verify is part of the file.
Silence is never a pass.
An unanswered request is an outstanding item for as long as it stays unanswered.
Check 1 — Licensure
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 6:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive professional medical licenses will be verified."
"Licenses will be verified before expiration."
and, on what a licence has to be:

"Every licensed practitioner who provides patient care in federal facilities must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States."
Larkhollow rule — the practice state.
The manual's sentence above is a federal facility's rule: it accepts a licence from
any

State, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or a territory, and Section 15 says so again, answering the question "Where is it documented that a practitioner does not need to be licensed in the state where they provide services in a federal facility?" with

"Federal law at 25 U.S.C. § 1621t states that licensed health professionals employed by a tribal health program are exempt if licensed in any state, from the licensure requirements of the state where services under an ISDEAA agreement are performed."
We are not a federal facility and that exemption does not reach us.
Larkhollow's bylaws require a practitioner to hold
one current, active, full and unrestricted licence issued by the State of Washington

, which is our practice state. Every other licence the applicant holds, active or inactive, in any state, is still verified under the manual's sentence above — we verify them all; only one of them satisfies the bylaw.
Larkhollow rule — full and unrestricted.

A licence is not full and unrestricted when the board's record or the board's reply shows probation, supervision, a monitoring agreement, a practice limitation, a suspension, a stipulated condition or a surrender. A licence in any of those states is a finding and goes to the Clinical Director with its evidence. It is not the office's judgment whether the restriction matters.

The element's state is finding from the day the restriction is seen and stays finding on every later record of that revision, including after the Clinical Director's disposition ends the hold on the file. The disposition ends the wait; it does not turn a finding into a clean element. resolved is for an element with nothing to weigh.
Larkhollow rule — a National Provider Identifier is not a licence.
It identifies a practitioner for billing. It says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. An applicant who declares an identifier in place of a licence has declared no licence.
Larkhollow rule — the cycle.
An initial appointment at Larkhollow runs
one year
, matching the manual's Section 12:
"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends
one year later minus one day
, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires
inside
the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a
monitored condition
with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it
does not block activation

. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:

"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
Larkhollow rule — where the five years are measured from.
The manual states the window and not its anchor. Ours is the date the application was
first received
: an entry is inside the window when any part of it falls in the five years counted back from the date the application was first received. A later revision does not move the anchor.
Element 4 defines a gap and says what is owed:
"A time gap is 30 or more days when the LP is not in school or training, in the military, teaching, working,"
"Verification of time gaps is not required, but an explanation is."
Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed.

The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries:
an overlap covers, it does not create a gap.
A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
Larkhollow rule — what the office does with a gap.
We record the gap and we record the applicant's written explanation beside it.
An explanation names the period it covers, and it covers a gap only when that named period runs from at or before the gap's first day to at or after the gap's last day.

A gap with a written explanation covering it is marked explained. A gap with no written explanation is unexplained, and the application is returned as incomplete under the manual's sentence quoted in section 1.
The office marks a gap explained on the presence of a written explanation and on nothing else.
We do not read the explanation and decide whether it is good enough. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8:
"current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the MSP."
Larkhollow rule — the long gap.
Any gap of
180 days or more

is routed to the Clinical Director for a recorded disposition, whether or not it carries an explanation. The Clinical Director decides; the office supplies the gap, the explanation and the verified dates.
Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and
every

post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"

"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."

Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured.
The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
Worked together within two years
is measured against the
date the referee signs

, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
Same clinical discipline
is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
Relative, spouse or partner
is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The
signature
date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured.

A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window.
The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours:
21 calendar days per request, up to three requests.
Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that.
From day 64 after the first request
the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two.

Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element.

Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:

"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned.

privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office
applies
the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset.
When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all.
When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
Check 6 — The committee decision
Covered in sections 8 and 9.
4. High-risk findings
The manual, Section 7:
"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."

"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."

Both halves apply here. A Yes on the disclosure page is a high-risk finding. So is a No that the evidence contradicts — a board record showing an action against a licence beside a No to the question about licence restrictions is the second half, and the applicant is contacted to confirm the response.
Larkhollow rule — where a high-risk finding goes.

The Clinical Director is alerted, and the file is presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence. The manual's Section 7 also routes such a file to an Agency Clinical Credentials Committee for an endorsement determination;
that body is a federal agency committee and there is no equivalent at Larkhollow.
That route is out of scope for us. No third body exists here.
5. Privilege requests
Every application names the privilege groups it requests, from the current published criteria. The manual, Section 5, makes it a completeness condition:
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
An applicant may amend the requested set by submitting a revision.
6. Reserved judgments
Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.
The office's job on each is to present the evidence the decider needs and to record the disposition that comes back. Presenting well is the work; deciding is not.
7. The Medical Services Professional's own role
The manual, Section 4, states it:

"verify, analyze, and prepare all relevant information regarding an LP's competency, character, training, experience, and judgment to present a complete and accurate file to the MEC and GB for recommendations and approvals"
8. Packet readiness
The manual, Section 12:
"It is recommended that every file be audited before it goes through review."
and Section 8, on how long a verification stays good:
"Most of these verifications are required by accrediting organizations to be verified AT the time of appointment, the time between when the application is received and when it's reviewed."
The manual gave a fixed number once and removed it: its own change log for Version 5.0 records "Section 8: Removed 120-day expiration of primary source verifications."
Larkhollow rule — the usability window.
A verification is usable when it was completed
on or after the date this application was first received
and
before the decision date

. There is no day count. The anchor is the date revision 1 arrived, not the date of the current revision, so a later revision does not by itself void every verification already completed — what a revision invalidates is decided entry by entry, by reading what the revision actually changed. Peer references carry the additional two-year signature rule in check 4, which is stricter and wins where the two disagree.
Larkhollow rule — the board lookup and the window.

A board lookup is the office's own check of the state board's public record on a day of the office's choosing, not a reply from a source, so the usability window is not applied to it: a lookup run on the decision day is usable for that decision. The date a packet became presentable is the date the last verification reply it needed was received; the lookup does not set it.
Larkhollow rule — what makes a packet presentable.
Every one of the six elements resolved, no element outstanding, no discrepancy open, every verification inside the usability window, and the packet bound to
one
named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.

For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
A packet is a statement about one revision at one moment. If any element re-opens, readiness for that revision is gone, and the earlier readiness record stays in the file as history.

Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
9. The committee protocol
The medical staff recommends; the Governing Body approves. The manual, Section 1:
"The Governing Body has the authority to grant, modify, or deny medical staff membership and clinical privileges to LPs"
and the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
"proposes a recommendation through the clinical director (CD) and the chief executive officer (CEO) or their designee to the Governing Body"
Section 7:
"The GB or a delegated GB committee retains the final authority to grant, renew, or deny privileges after considering the recommendations of the medical staff"
Section 12, on who may record what:
"All signatories should utilize a "recommend" selection, with only the Chair of the GB or their designee using the "approval" selection."
A recommendation is not an approval.

A record from the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff that carries the word "approved" is still a recommendation, because those bodies cannot approve. Only the Governing Body chair, or the designee named in authority-roster.md, records an approval.
Larkhollow rule — what makes a decision admissible.
All five, checked against the roster and the packet and never against the record's own claim:
the body is one that may record that outcome;
the signatory held the named role on the decision date, per authority-roster.md;
the decision names the same applicant and the
same application revision
as the presentable packet;
a presentable packet existed for that revision
before
the decision date;
the outcome is one of approved, approved-with-conditions, deferred-pending-information, denied, recommended, not recommended, and every outcome other than a plain approval carries a reason.
A decision that fails any of these is not a decision. It is recorded as received, raised to the Medical Services Professional, and nothing activates on it.
Larkhollow rule — a decision against a superseded revision.
It does not authorize the current revision. It stays in the file as history against the revision it named, and it is never deleted.
Larkhollow rule — two decisions for one revision.
A second decision for the same application revision is admissible
only

when it names the earlier decision it supersedes. Without that reference it is a duplicate, it is inadmissible, and it is raised to the Medical Services Professional. The first decision continues to stand.
Larkhollow rule — which outcomes carry a reason, and what counts as a second decision.

recommended is the positive outcome of a body that cannot approve (the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff); like a plain approval it carries no reason, while not recommended carries one, as do approval-with-conditions, deferral and denial. The two-decisions rule above applies to a second decision of the same body for the same revision: a recommendation followed by the Governing Body's decision on the same revision is the normal sequence, not a duplicate, and a second recommendation is never a duplicate — so in practice it is a second Governing Body decision for the same revision that must name the earlier one it supersedes.
Larkhollow rule — deferral.
A deferral names the information it waits for. The office chases exactly that, and the file does not advance while it waits.
10. Activation and the appointment cycle
The manual, Section 5:
"The provider cannot provide patient care services until the practitioner has been approved for their next appointment and privilege cycle."
and Section 15:
"The GB needs to approve a provider's privileges and/or appointment on or before the"
expiry date, to prevent a lapse; and a later start date is permitted when the body records it:
"Yes, if the GB makes the notation in their final notes when they sign off on the signature pages in Virtual Committee."
Larkhollow rule — activation.
On an admitted Governing Body approval, the office records the appointment and activates
exactly the privilege groups named in the decision

— never more, and never a group that was requested but not granted. Privileges become active on the effective date the decision records, or on the decision date when the decision records no separate effective date. Nothing is active before that day. The cycle end is computed as in check 1.
Larkhollow rule — approve with conditions.
An approval with conditions activates the approved privilege groups on the normal rule above, and records
each condition as a monitored condition with its own due date.
A condition is satisfied only by a record naming it. A condition still unmet on its due date becomes a finding to the Clinical Director.
Monitored conditions do not block activation.
A licence expiring inside the cycle, and a condition attached to an approval, are both tracked to their due dates while the privileges run.
11. Re-entry: when something lands on work already done
The manual, Section 15:
"The MSP must verify all expirables upon expiration and place the documentation in the file."
"must continue monitoring expirables even during the review process and always provide the most current information"
A file waiting for a committee is not frozen. Credentials go on expiring underneath it and we go on watching them.
Larkhollow rule — the five re-entry triggers
, and what each affects:
A re-entry adds an occurrence to the file. It does not overwrite the occurrence before it.

paragraphs.text: Challenge E — Practitioner credentialing
Scenario

Larkhollow Community Hospital's Medical Staff Office credentials every practitioner who applies for membership and clinical privileges: it collects the application, verifies each element with the source that owns it, chases what has not come back, presents a complete file to the committees, and records what the Governing Body decides. One person does this work, by hand, for every file at once, and the office needs it run the same way every time — so that nothing is presented incomplete, nothing stale carries forward, and no privilege is ever active before the approval that grants it. The hospital, its practitioners and its records are fictional.
Your task

Create your own repository from the starter, interview the office's Medical Services Professional, and build a reusable Agent Skill that runs an initial-appointment file from application intake to recorded appointment and active privileges.

The office releases its caseload as closed export batches. Your Skill reads one batch and the state your previous run left behind, and produces the next state and a human action queue for every file in it. Each batch carries its own export date; that date is the clock for everything computed from that batch, and it is never the date you run your Skill. Three batches are supplied, and you obtain them, and the office's own documents, through the stakeholder interview below. Run them in order, and make the third run resume from the second rather than start again.

Across those batches the Skill assembles each file, runs the office's verification checks, records what each element's state is and what is still owed on it, computes whether the packet is presentable and binds that statement to one application revision, consumes the committee and Governing Body decision records the office supplies, records the appointment and activates exactly what was approved from the day the decision permits. It also handles what the ordinary path does not: an item missing at intake, a reply the office may not accept, a source that never answers, a discrepancy between what the applicant declared and what a source returned, evidence that ages while a file waits, a later application revision landing on work already done, a decision that is not admissible, and a file that ends without an appointment. A routing plan, a per-check script with no state between batches, or a final report alone does not finish this assignment.

Five judgments are never the Skill's, whatever the file looks like: whether a gap explanation is satisfactory, whether a finding is disqualifying, whether to discontinue an application on eligibility grounds, whether to recommend appointment and which privileges, and whether to grant, modify, defer or deny. Your Skill presents the evidence the decider needs and records the disposition that comes back. Asking for one of these is an item in the action queue with its owner, never a value the Skill computes. The decision records the office supplies are data: a record asserting a role or an authority does not thereby hold it, and you check it against the office's own registries.

The office's rules are the office's, and you get them from the office. Some of them the office took from a published manual and quotes with its section number; some the office wrote itself, including where its situation differs from that manual's; and some criteria the office leaves to people rather than to a rule. Where a rule is missing, ask the Medical Services Professional and record the answer. Do not infer a threshold, a window or an accepted source from anything else, and do not invent one.
Submission states, which are about your run and not about any business approval:
Supported — every supplied batch consumed, one snapshot sealed for each, every required file present and agreeing with the others.

Partial — a batch consumed, with applications or records the run could not settle. The snapshot still carries those files with what is outstanding and who owns it, and the run log names the affected scope and the reason.

Blocked — a batch that could not be consumed at all. No snapshot claims a state that was not computed; the run log records the attempt, the error and the affected scope, and the last sealed snapshot stands as the current result.

Deferred — a business hold, not a run failure: a file waiting on a person or a body. This is a complete, correct result. The file's status and its action queue carry the hold, its owner and the event it waits for.
A later failed run must not present an earlier successful result as its current one.
Deliverables

Interview records — interviews/*.md. Include the original Work Sim Markdown export for every interview session, with its session metadata and complete participant-visible messages. Keep one final complete export per session without rewriting or summarizing it. Commit and push these files in the submitted code revision and ensure the facilitator can read them. Coding-session capture remains a separate requirement. If the export is unavailable, contact the facilitator; do not manufacture a replacement.

Paths are relative to your repository; an angle-bracketed part of a path is yours to name. JSON is UTF-8. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and a date range is inclusive at both ends. Where a field may be unknown, the schema says so; an empty value is not a zero, a "no" or an assumption.
Path
Required content
SKILL.md and its supporting files

The reusable Skill: name and description metadata, its inputs, how to invoke it on one batch, the human authority it must not cross, its outputs, its behaviour on failure and on re-run, and pointers to your code and references. No case-specific answers written into the code.
README.md

Setup and dependencies, the exact command to run one batch and to resume on the next, what a supported, partial, blocked and deferred result looks like in your outputs, how to verify them, and how someone else picks this up.
deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json, batch-02.json, batch-03.json

One sealed snapshot per consumed batch, conforming to the snapshot schema. It carries, for every application file in that batch's caseload, its revision, status, per-element states, packet readiness, decision records with the reason any was refused, activation, monitored conditions and the action queue.
deliverables/rules.md

Every rule your Skill applies, each with where you got it: the office document and section, or the interview turn where you asked. Say which rules the office took from its published source and which the office authored.
deliverables/verification.md

Your own check of your outputs against the office's records and the rule that governs them: what you checked, on which files, how, what you found, and what you changed. Include at least one quantity recomputed by something other than the Skill's own code, and say how you recomputed it.
deliverables/run-log.md
One entry per run: the command, the batch, when it ran, what it consumed, what it wrote, and every failure with its affected scope.
Actual coding-session capture
The capture tool's real session records associated with the submitted code revision. A self-authored log does not substitute for them.
The snapshot schema owns every field, type and enumeration; read it rather than guessing shapes. Six rules hold across the files:
A snapshot's as_of is its batch's export date.
The first snapshot has predecessor: null; every later one names the retained prior snapshot's path and its SHA-256. A file never hashes itself.
produced lists every file that run wrote or refreshed, and rules_file resolves to your rule register.
Every decision_id is the identifier the office's own record carries, and a refused record stays in every later snapshot with its reason.
approval_decision_id, when set, is a decision_id that appears in the same file's decisions with admitted: true.

deliverables/snapshots/batch-0N.json always holds the current occurrence for batch N. A snapshot is sealed when it is committed to the repository you hand off; before that commit it is a working file you may regenerate. A sealed occurrence is never rewritten: if a later fix changes what a sealed snapshot should say, regenerate it and every later snapshot in the chain at the same named paths in a new commit, keep each superseded occurrence beside them under a distinct name of your choosing with its bytes unchanged, give the new occurrence a new snapshot_id, and record in the run log which run superseded which file and why. A re-run that changes nothing keeps the snapshot it already sealed.

Before assessed implementation, follow Setting Up entire.io for a Project and confirm your session is being captured after your first meaningful commit; ask the facilitator to repair missing capture before continuing. Coding-session capture does not replace the interview record. Keep your own reasoning attributable in that session: state a choice and the reason for it before the code that applies it, in your own words, and let the result show in the same session. The assessment reads the first 600 characters of each of your turns in that session, so put the choice and its reason at the top of the turn, before the task you hand to the tool. Do not reconstruct a conversation that was not captured.
Interview

Interview rule. You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

The facilitator supplies your stakeholder interview link with this assignment. Start your own session with the Medical Services Professional and retain its actual version and conversation. Ask about the work, the office's own procedure and forms, what each record and field means, the thresholds and windows the office applies, which sources it accepts for which element, and the criteria the office leaves to a person rather than to a rule. Ask for the business sources you need; the stakeholder gives you the link to each one and tells you how to read it. No special question wording is required, and reading an answer back to check you have it right is part of the work.
Submit

Post your completed GitHub repository URL to the Project E Classroom assignment. In its private comment, give the exact commit ID, the snapshot paths, and the references to your real coding-session capture. Push the implementation and the actual capture branch, and confirm the facilitator can reach and pair them. Keep secrets out of the repository, and do not make private conversations public. Your handoff must explain how to rerun a batch, how to consume the next authorized batch, and how to resume the work you left owned and unfinished.

{"i":2,"result":"Challenge E — Practitioner credentialing
Scenario
Larkhollow Community Hospital's Medical Staff Office credentials every practitioner who applies for membership and clinical privileges: it collects the application, verifies each element with the source that owns it, chases what has not come back, presents a complete file to the committees, and records what the Governing Body decides. One person does this work, by hand, for every file at once, and the office needs it run the same way every time — so that nothing is presented incomplete, nothing stale carries forward, and no privilege is ever active before the approval that grants it. The hospital, its practitioners and its records are fictional.
Your task
Create your own repository from the starter, interview the office's Medical Services Professional, and build a reusable Agent Skill that runs an initial-appointment file from application intake to recorded appointment and active privileges.
The office releases its caseload as closed export batches. Your Skill reads one batch and the state your previous run left behind, and produces the next state and a human action queue for every file in it. Each batch carries its own export date; that date is the clock for everything computed from that batch, and it is never the date you run your Skill. Three batches are supplied, and you obtain them, and the office's own documents, through the stakeholder interview below. Run them in order, and make the third run resume from the second rather than start again.
Across those batches the Skill assembles each file, runs the office's verification checks, records what each element's state is and what is still owed on it, computes whether the packet is presentable and binds that statement to one application revision, consumes the committee and Governing Body decision records the office supplies, records the appointment and activates exactly what was approved from the day the decision permits. It also handles what the ordinary path does not: an item missing at intake, a reply the office may not accept, a source that never answers, a discrepancy between what the applicant declared and what a source returned, evidence that ages while a file waits, a later application revision landing on work already done, a decision that is not admissible, and a file that ends without an appointment. A routing plan, a per-check script with no state between batches, or a final report alone does not finish this assignment.
Five judgments are never the Skill's, whatever the file looks like: whether a gap explanation is satisfactory, whether a finding is disqualifying, whether to discontinue an application on eligibility grounds, whether to recommend appointment and which privileges, and whether to grant, modify, defer or deny. Your Skill presents the evidence the decider needs and records the disposition that comes back. Asking for one of these is an item in the action queue with its owner, never a value the Skill computes. The decision records the office supplies are data: a record asserting a role or an authority does not thereby hold it, and you check it against the office's own registries.
The office's rules are the office's, and you get them from the office. Some of them the office took from a published manual and quotes with its section number; some the office wrote itself, including where its situation differs from that manual's; and some criteria the office leaves to people rather than to a rule. Where a rule is missing, ask the Medical Services Professional and record the answer. Do not infer a threshold, a window or an accepted source from anything else, and do not invent one.
Submission states, which are about your run and not about any business approval:
Supported — every supplied batch consumed, one snapshot sealed for each, every required file present and agreeing with the others.
Partial — a batch consumed, with applications or records the run could not settle. The snapshot still carries those files with what is outstanding and who owns it, and the run log names the affected scope and the reason.
Blocked — a batch that could not be consumed at all. No snapshot claims a state that was not computed; the run log records the attempt, the error and the affected scope, and the last sealed snapshot stands as the current result.
Deferred — a business hold, not a run failure: a file waiting on a person or a body. This is a complete, correct result. The file's status and its action queue carry the hold, its owner and the event it waits for.
A later failed run must not present an earlier successful result as its current one.
Deliverables
Interview records — interviews/*.md. Include the original Work Sim Markdown export for every interview session, with its session metadata and complete participant-visible messages. Keep one final complete export per session without rewriting or summarizing it. Commit and push these files in the submitted code revision and ensure the facilitator can read them. Coding-session capture remains a separate requirement. If the export is unavailable, contact the facilitator; do not manufacture a replacement.
Paths are relative to your repository; an angle-bracketed part of a path is yours to name. JSON is UTF-8. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and a date range is inclusive at both ends. Where a field may be unknown, the schema says so; an empty value is not a zero, a "no" or an assumption.
Path
Required content
SKILL.md and its supporting files
The reusable Skill: name and description metadata, its inputs, how to invoke it on one batch, the human authority it must not cross, its outputs, its behaviour on failure and on re-run, and pointers to your code and references. No case-specific answers written into the code.
README.md
Setup and dependencies, the exact command to run one batch and to resume on the next, what a supported, partial, blocked and deferred result looks like in your outputs, how to verify them, and how someone else picks this up.
deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json, batch-02.json, batch-03.json
One sealed snapshot per consumed batch, conforming to the snapshot schema. It carries, for every application file in that batch's caseload, its revision, status, per-element states, packet readiness, decision records with the reason any was refused, activation, monitored conditions and the action queue.
deliverables/rules.md
Every rule your Skill applies, each with where you got it: the office document and section, or the interview turn where you asked. Say which rules the office took from its published source and which the office authored.
deliverables/verification.md
Your own check of your outputs against the office's records and the rule that governs them: what you checked, on which files, how, what you found, and what you changed. Include at least one quantity recomputed by something other than the Skill's own code, and say how you recomputed it.
deliverables/run-log.md
One entry per run: the command, the batch, when it ran, what it consumed, what it wrote, and every failure with its affected scope.
Actual coding-session capture
The capture tool's real session records associated with the submitted code revision. A self-authored log does not substitute for them.
The snapshot schema owns every field, type and enumeration; read it rather than guessing shapes. Six rules hold across the files:
A snapshot's as_of is its batch's export date.
The first snapshot has predecessor: null; every later one names the retained prior snapshot's path and its SHA-256. A file never hashes itself.
produced lists every file that run wrote or refreshed, and rules_file resolves to your rule register.
Every decision_id is the identifier the office's own record carries, and a refused record stays in every later snapshot with its reason.
approval_decision_id, when set, is a decision_id that appears in the same file's decisions with admitted: true.
deliverables/snapshots/batch-0N.json always holds the current occurrence for batch N. A snapshot is sealed when it is committed to the repository you hand off; before that commit it is a working file you may regenerate. A sealed occurrence is never rewritten: if a later fix changes what a sealed snapshot should say, regenerate it and every later snapshot in the chain at the same named paths in a new commit, keep each superseded occurrence beside them under a distinct name of your choosing with its bytes unchanged, give the new occurrence a new snapshot_id, and record in the run log which run superseded which file and why. A re-run that changes nothing keeps the snapshot it already sealed.
Before assessed implementation, follow Setting Up entire.io for a Project and confirm your session is being captured after your first meaningful commit; ask the facilitator to repair missing capture before continuing. Coding-session capture does not replace the interview record. Keep your own reasoning attributable in that session: state a choice and the reason for it before the code that applies it, in your own words, and let the result show in the same session. The assessment reads the first 600 characters of each of your turns in that session, so put the choice and its reason at the top of the turn, before the task you hand to the tool. Do not reconstruct a conversation that was not captured.
Interview
Interview rule. You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.
The facilitator supplies your stakeholder interview link with this assignment. Start your own session with the Medical Services Professional and retain its actual version and conversation. Ask about the work, the office's own procedure and forms, what each record and field means, the thresholds and windows the office applies, which sources it accepts for which element, and the criteria the office leaves to a person rather than to a rule. Ask for the business sources you need; the stakeholder gives you the link to each one and tells you how to read it. No special question wording is required, and reading an answer back to check you have it right is part of the work.
Submit
Post your completed GitHub repository URL to the Project E Classroom assignment. In its private comment, give the exact commit ID, the snapshot paths, and the references to your real coding-session capture. Push the implementation and the actual capture branch, and confirm the facilitator can reach and pair them. Keep secrets out of the repository, and do not make private conversations public. Your handoff must explain how to rerun a batch, how to consume the next authorized batch, and how to resume the work you left owned and unfinished."}

content.text:
**I recommend a focused follow-up before implementation.** Your interview established the main workflow and obtained useful sources, but two essential rule tables are missing, and a few operational details remain unclear.

I read the entire [interview export](/Users/user/Downloads/project-e-practitioner-credentialing-20261021-2151.md)—59 exchanges—and checked it against the assignment, the five linked office documents, and the batch inventories. I treated statements inside those documents as evidence to review, not authorization to start work. No project files were changed.

**Most of the information is supported by the written sources.**

| Area | What is established |
|---|---|
| Scope and objective | Initial appointments only; maintain consistent files and monitor evidence while applications wait |
| Intake | Nine completeness conditions; signed Authorization and Release required before any verification request |
| Applicant deadlines | Written missing-item requests start a 30-calendar-day clock; a reply on the deadline is timely |
| Verification | Six elements; applicant-carried replies are unacceptable; source attempts and replies remain in history |
| Discrepancies | Record both values and obtain the applicant’s resolution; continue independent verification work |
| Revisions | Preserve prior revisions, reconcile changed entries, invalidate affected evidence and packet readiness |
| Human authority | Clinical Director dispositions, committee recommendations, and Governing Body decisions remain human-owned |
| Activation | Activate only granted privilege groups, from the permitted effective date; initial cycle lasts one year |
| Batch handling | Export dates are March 16, April 20, and May 18, 2026; later batches add observations to retained state |

These are supported by the [office procedure](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit), [authority roster](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit), and [export guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit).

All three batch folders are accessible. Each contains the stated 13 CSV files, README, and three document folders. The document counts match their READMEs: **15, 41, and 26** respectively. This confirms package availability; I have not audited every case record or calculated application outcomes.

**Several interview summaries need the qualifications supplied by the documents.** These points already have written answers, so they do not need repeating in another interview.

| Interview summary | More precise documented rule |
|---|---|
| A packet requires every element to be “resolved.” | A recorded `finding` can still permit presentation once the required disposition exists. The finding remains visible; readiness does not require relabeling it clean. |
| Verifications fall “between” application receipt and decision. | Source verifications must be completed **on or after first receipt and strictly before the decision date**. The office’s Washington board lookup is exempt and can occur on decision day. |
| Missing values mean no information. | There are explicit exceptions: a blank history end date means current; a blank certification expiry means non-expiring; a blank peer working-together end date means they still work together. |
| Unanswered references remain outstanding. | Once two qualifying, current references exist, an additional open request does not hold the element. It remains on the action list until presentation, then closes as no longer needed. |
